The Government of Maldives reaffirms its commitment and support to China's national unity and to the one-China Policy. The Maldives' firm conviction of one-China policy is guided by the principles of respect for sovereignty, territorial integrity and non-interference in the internal affairs of states and considers Taiwan as an integral part of the People's Republic of China.

China is a very important development partner for the Maldives and the Government of Maldives will continue to work with the Government of the People's Republic of China to strengthen the close ties of friendship and co-operation existing between our two countries.

ENDS.

en.title: First Non- Resident Ambassador of Maldives to the Philippines presents Credentials to Philippines President
en.description: 10 June 2013, Male'; The first Ambassador of Maldives to the Philippines, His Excellency Hussain Shihab presented his Letter of Credence as Non-Resident Ambassador, to the President of the Philippines, His Excellency Benigno Simeon Cojuangco Aquino III today. The ceremony was held at the official…
en.body:
10 June 2013, Male'; The first Ambassador of Maldives to the Philippines, His Excellency Hussain Shihab presented his Letter of Credence as Non-Resident Ambassador, to the President of the Philippines, His Excellency Benigno Simeon Cojuangco Aquino III today. The ceremony was held at the official residence of the President of the Philippines "the Malacañan Palace".

During the ceremony, President Aquino conveyed his greetings to the President and the people of the Republic of Maldives, and discussed ways of strengthening the close bilateral ties between the two countries.

During the discussions, Ambassador Shihab conveyed greetings from the President and people of the Maldives, to the President and the people of Philippines and discussed ways of further strengthening the close relations and expanding economic activities between the two countries. High Commissioner Shihab also noted that there are a number of Philippine expatriates working in the tourism industry of the Maldives providing valuable contributions to the sector.

After the presentation, President Aquino welcomed the twelve Ambassadors of the twelve countries who presented credentials today. A reception was also hosted by the President in honor of the new Ambassadors.

Ambassador Shihab is scheduled to meet with the Secretary for Foreign Affairs of the Philippines tomorrow and will be participating in the Independence Day celebrations to be hosted by the Philippines President on 12 June 2013.

ENDS.

en.title: Maldives participation in the 23rd Session of the Human Rights Council
en.description: 10th June 2013, Male'; The Maldives has continued to engage actively on all human rights issues within the remits of the ongoing 23rd Session of the Human Rights Council in Geneva.Among the priorities this year, the Maldives welcomed the Report of the Special Rapporteur on the Independence of…
en.body:
10th June 2013, Male'; The Maldives has continued to engage actively on all human rights issues within the remits of the ongoing 23rd Session of the Human Rights Council in Geneva.Among the priorities this year, the Maldives welcomed the Report of the Special Rapporteur on the Independence of Judges and Lawyers, Ms. Gabriella Knaul following her visit to the Maldives and expressed its hope for continued dialogue with the Council and its mechanisms. In its statement, the Maldives acknowledged that it faced structural deficiencies and resource constrains in addressing the issues raised in the report, and reiterated its commitment to acclimatize and implement the recommendations of the Special Rapporteur and requested the support of the international human rights mechanism and international partners in implementing them.

It actively engaged with other delegations during the consultations on a resolution to end violence against women, and participated in discussions to support national human rights institutions and on the independence and impartiality of judges and lawyers of which the Maldives was a member of the Core Group.

During the session, the Maldives delivered statements on the Panel Discussion on the Role of Parliaments in promoting human rights- a panel co-sponsored by the Maldives and the annual full day discussions on women's rights. Further the Maldives delegation participated in the interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on Peaceful Assembly and Association, the Special Rapporteur on Occupied Palestinian Territories and the Special Rapporteur on Violence Against Women to name a few.

The 23rd Session of the Human Rights Council commenced on 27th May 2013 and will continue until 14th June 2013. The Maldives is being represented at the session by the Permanent Mission of the Republic of Maldives to the United Nations Offices in Geneva.

ENDS

en.title: President Meets Jordanian King
en.description: 05 June 2013, Male'; President Dr Mohamed Waheed on Tuesday made a stopover visit to Jordan en route to Palestine. During his visit, President Waheed met with the King of Jordan Abdulla II and discussed bilateral relations between the two countries.
en.body:
05 June 2013, Male'; President Dr Mohamed Waheed on Tuesday made a stopover visit to Jordan en route to Palestine. During his visit, President Waheed met with the King of Jordan Abdulla II and discussed bilateral relations between the two countries.

Discussions at the meeting were mainly focused on issues of concern to the Muslim world and ways to strengthen the existing close ties between the two countries.

President Waheed praised King Abdulla's efforts to solidify cooperation among Muslim countries and his efforts to bring peace and stability in the region.

The President also invited King Abdulla to make a visit to the Maldives. He also explored possibilities to strengthen ties with Jordan in economic and other fields.

ENDS.

en.title: President Waheed Meets Palestinian President
en.description: 05 June 2013, Male'; During his visit to Palestine, to officiate the 4th Islamic Conference of Bait Al Maqdis, President Dr Mohamed Waheed on Tuesday met with the President of Palestine, Dr Mahmoud Abbas.
en.body:
05 June 2013, Male'; During his visit to Palestine, to officiate the 4th Islamic Conference of Bait Al Maqdis, President Dr Mohamed Waheed on Tuesday met with the President of Palestine, Dr Mahmoud Abbas.

At the meeting, the two leaders discussed bilateral ties that exist between the two countries.

Speaking at the meeting, President Waheed thanked President Abbas for the invitation and said it was a great honour for him to visit Palestine.

He also expressed confidence that his visit to Palestine would boost the close fraternal relations between the two countries.

President Abbas thanked the Maldivian government and people for the strong support to the Palestinian struggle. He also briefed President Waheed on the latest development in the region and on the peace process.

After the meeting, the two leaders held a joint press conference, where they briefed the media on the discussions held during their meeting.

At the press conference, President Waheed said he held "fruitful" talks with Abbas.

"Our people have always stood with the Palestinian people," he said.

"Our people are looking for solutions to the difficulties facing the Palestinian people and support the idea of the two-state solution on the 1967 borders so that there will be peace in the Middle East."

ENDS.

en.title: Signing of the Exchange of Letters regarding the construction of the Islands Stretch Road in Laamu Atoll under assistance from China
en.description: 04 June 2013, Male':The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the People's Republic of China, today signed agreement to construct the ‘Islands Stretch Road' in Laamu Atoll.The road will be of about 15 kilometers, starting from the northern end of Gan Island and, end at the…
en.body:
04 June 2013, Male':The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the People's Republic of China, today signed agreement to construct the ‘Islands Stretch Road' in Laamu Atoll.The road will be of about 15 kilometers, starting from the northern end of Gan Island and, end at the southern end of Fonadhoo Island.

During a ceremony held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Exchange of Letters was signed by His Excellency Mr. Abdul Azeez Yoosuf, Ambassador- at-Large and His Excellency Mr. Yu Hongyao, Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to the Republic of Maldives. Ambassador Azeez also thanked the people and the Government of China for it's continued assistance and support to the socio-economic development of the Maldives and expressed.Speaking at the ceremony, Ambassador Yu Hongyao highlighted the close friendship between the two countries and expressed hope that the construction of the road would bring development to region and benefit the people of Laamu Atoll.

The signing ceremony was witnessed by senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Housing and Infrastructure, Ministry of Finance and Treasury and the officials of the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Male'.

ENDS

en.title: Prime Minister of Thailand concludes her visit to the Maldives
en.description: 03 June 2013, Male'; Prime Minister of Thailand, Yingluck Shinawatra has concluded her visit to the Maldives, this afternoon. Shee was seeing off at the airport by Vice President Mohamed Waheed Deen.
en.body:
03 June 2013, Male'; Prime Minister of Thailand, Yingluck Shinawatra has concluded her visit to the Maldives, this afternoon. Shee was seeing off at the airport by Vice President Mohamed Waheed Deen.

Prime Minister Shinawatra arrived in the Maldives on Saturday. During her visit to the Maldives, she met with President Waheed and other state officials and discussed bilateral ties with the Maldives and Thailand.

A joint statement on the occasion of the official visit of Prime Minister Shinawatra to the Maldives was issued today.

The statement outlines key areas of discussions that were held between the two countries and some of the outcomes of those discussions.

According to the joint statement, the two leaders expressed satisfaction at the strong and growing trade relations between the two countries and agreed to double trade volume bilateral trade between the two countries by the year 2018.

Recognizing that people-to-people contacts are an important part of the relations between the two countries, the Thai side invited more Maldivian people to visit Thailand for medical treatment. As such, it was agreed that the conclusion of a visa waiver agreement in the near future would increase people-to-people contact.

The Joint Statement also highlighted the seven agreements that were signed between the two countries during the Prime Minister's visit.

According to the statement, both leaders expressed satisfaction with the outcome of the official visit.

ENDS.

en.title: Foreign Minister Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah calls on the Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Thailand, Her Excellency Yingluck Shinawatra
en.description: 2 June 2013, Male':Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, His Excellency Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah paid a courtesy call on Her Excellency Yingluck Shinawatra, Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Thailand today.
en.body:
2 June 2013, Male':Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, His Excellency Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah paid a courtesy call on Her Excellency Yingluck Shinawatra, Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Thailand today.

During the meeting, held at the Kurumba Maldives, Her Excellency Ms. Yingluck Shinawatra assured His Excellency Dr Abdul Samad Abdulla of the commitment of the Government of Thailand to strengthen close ties with the Maldives.The Prime Minister added that establishment of the Joint Commission between the two countries would be a positive avenue to discuss promotion of investments, trade, and to explore other avenues for collaboration.

Reflecting on the discussions at the official talks held between the two Governments yesterday, His Excellency Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah said he looks forward to working closely with the Thai Government to further consolidate and diversify the bilateral relations between the Maldives and Thailand.

ENDS

en.title: President and First Lady host a banquet in honour of the visiting Thai PM
en.description: 01 June 2013, Male'; President Dr Mohamed Waheed and First Lady Madam Ilham Hussain have hosted a banquet in honour of the Prime Minister of Thailand Yingluck Shinawatra, who is currently in the Maldives on an official visit.
en.body:
01 June 2013, Male'; President Dr Mohamed Waheed and First Lady Madam Ilham Hussain have hosted a banquet in honour of the Prime Minister of Thailand Yingluck Shinawatra, who is currently in the Maldives on an official visit.

In his remarks at the banquet, President Waheed said that the Prime Minister's visit to the Maldives has enabled the two countries to forge a "partnership that would create new horizons" in the relationship between the Maldives and Thailand.

He said:

"It is a partnership that would also create new opportunities for the peoples of our two countries to explore their entrepreneurial talents".

Stressing that the relationship between the Maldives and Thailand was built on shared values and interests, President Waheed also said the two countries also face similar challenges.
"And as our countries move towards democratic growth and look towards sustained economic advancement and stability, we face similar challenges", he said.

In his speech, President Waheed also praised the Prime Minister for the "bold steps" she had taken and "the new vision" she has set out for Thailand.

In her remarks, the Prime Minister commended Maldives's efforts to combat climate change. She said Thai government would extend its support and cooperation to the Maldives in this endeavor.

ENDS.

en.title: Government intends to double Thai investments in the Maldives in the next five years - President Waheed
en.description: 01 June 2013, Male'; President Dr Mohamed Waheed has said the government intends to double the amount of Thai investments in the Maldives. He made this statement while speaking at a joint press conference with the visiting Thai Prime Minister Yingluck Shinawatra, following talks with the Thai Prime…
en.body:
01 June 2013, Male'; President Dr Mohamed Waheed has said the government intends to double the amount of Thai investments in the Maldives. He made this statement while speaking at a joint press conference with the visiting Thai Prime Minister Yingluck Shinawatra, following talks with the Thai Prime Minister. The press conference was held this evening at Mulee-aage.

In his remarks, President Waheed noted that there were already significant Thai investments in the tourism sector. The President discussed with the Thai Prime Minister "the need for expanding investment in other sectors, such as food processing, infrastructure development, construction, and health care," he told the media.

Stating that nearly 30 per cent of Maldives' exports go to Thailand, the President said, "we would like to increase that number significantly in the coming years".

The President praised the role of Thailand in the ASEAN, and noted as the current chair of the South Asian Association of Regional Cooperation, the Maldives wanted to further strengthen the relations between the two bodies.

In her statement to the media, Prime Minister Shinawatra committed to further consolidating and diversifying the bilateral relations between the Maldives and Thailand.

ENDS.

en.title: Maldivian and Thai Governments hold Official Talks
en.description: 01 June 2013, Male'; The governments of the Maldives and Thailand have held official talks, led by President Mohamed Waheed and Prime Minister Yingluck Shinawatra of Thailand, during the latter's visit to the Maldives. The talks took place at Mulee-aage on Saturday afternoon.
en.body:
01 June 2013, Male'; The governments of the Maldives and Thailand have held official talks, led by President Mohamed Waheed and Prime Minister Yingluck Shinawatra of Thailand, during the latter's visit to the Maldives. The talks took place at Mulee-aage on Saturday afternoon.

The discussions were focused on further expanding and diversifying the relations between the two countries in areas such as fisheries, agriculture, construction sectors.

As a measure of further strengthening trade and economic relations, the President reiterated Maldives' interest to ease travel to Thailand by signing a visa waiver agreement.

Prime Minister Shinawatra shared Thai government's interest in expanding trade and other sectors. She discussed Thai government's plan to increasing cooperation in the areas of agriculture, fishery, health and human resources development.

Before the official talks, the President and Prime Minister Shinawatra met separately and discussed bilateral relations.

Following the official talks, the governments of Thailand and Maldives signed seven agreements. The seven agreements are:

1.Comprehensive Framework Agreement on Cooperation between Maldives and Thailand

2.MoU On The Establishment Of Bilateral Consultations Between The Ministry Of Foreign Affairs Of The Kingdom Of Thailand And The Ministry Of Foreign Affairs Of The Republic Of Maldives

3.Transfer Of Prisoners Between Thailand And Maldives

4.Trade and Economic Cooperation Agreement between the Government of Maldives and the Government of the Kingdom of Thailand

5.MoU between the Maldives National Chamber of Commerce and the Joint Standing Committee on Commerce, Industry and Banking.

6.MoU between ADK Hospital and Thonburi Hospital.

7.MoU between Loxley Public Company Limited and AGT International and Ministry of Home Affairs of Maldives on Safe City.

ENDS.

en.title: Thai Prime Minister to Visit the Maldives
en.description: 30 May 2013, Male'; The Prime Minister of Thailand, Ms. Yingluck Shinawatra is scheduled to make an official visit to the Maldives from 1st to 3rd June on the invitation of President Dr. Mohamed Waheed.
en.body:
30 May 2013, Male'; The Prime Minister of Thailand, Ms. Yingluck Shinawatra is scheduled to make an official visit to the Maldives from 1st to 3rd June on the invitation of President Dr. Mohamed Waheed.

During her visit, the Prime Minister will call on President Waheed and the two leaders will hold official talks on the bilateral relations between the Maldives and Thailand. Seven agreements on mutual cooperation between the two countries will be also concluded during the visit. President Dr. Mohamed Waheed will host an Official Dinner in honour of the visiting Prime Minister.

Diplomatic relations between the Maldives and Thailand were established in June 1979. Thailand is one of the largest trading partners of the Maldives accounting for nearly thirty percent of the country's exports. In 2012 the trade volume between the Maldives and Thailand totaled over 100 million US Dollars.

ENDS.

en.title: "Political differences in the international community must not be a basis for indecisiveness":Maldives expresses concern on the escalation of the Syrian conflict
en.description: 29 May 2013, Geneva; The Maldives today participated in an Urgent Debate held in the Human Rights Council concerning the deteriorating situation of human rights in the Syrian Arab Republic, and the recent killings in the city of Al-Qusayr.
en.body:
29 May 2013, Geneva; The Maldives today participated in an Urgent Debate held in the Human Rights Council concerning the deteriorating situation of human rights in the Syrian Arab Republic, and the recent killings in the city of Al-Qusayr.

In delivering her remarks to the Human Rights Council, H.E. Ms. Iruthisham Adam, Permanent Representatives of the Republic of Maldives strongly reiterated the call by the Government of Maldives to cease all violence and to reach a negotiated settlement to end the conflict. The Maldives also condemned in the strongest terms the systematic and gross violations that are taking place in Al-Qusayr, and the use of disproportionate force in residential areas by the Syrian Government, including aerial attacks and indiscriminate shelling of civilian populations in the city.

In her statement, Ambassador Adam expressed alarm on the participation of non-state actors from neighboring countries in the conflict which now threatens regional peace and stability. "It is most disconcerting that the conflict in Syria and all its maladies are spilling over to neighbouring countries, with wide implications for the peace and stability of the entire region. We call on the international community, especially the United Nations Security Council to implement urgently enforcement measures to give effect to its resolutions on this conflict. Political differences in the international community must not be a basis for indecisiveness, especially when thousands of lives have been lost and the undoing of the Syrian State continues before our eyes. The humanitarian and human cost of the conflict has already become immeasurable", said the Ambassador.

The Maldives also welcomed international efforts to hold an international conference in Geneva in June 2013, aimed at finding a political solution to the conflict and expressed its commitment to support all such efforts to end the violence.

The Human Rights Council adopted the resolution, which was tabled jointly by Qatar, Turkey and the United States, with overwhelming support. The Maldives both co-sponsored the resolution and voted in favour of it.

The situation in Syria continues to deteriorate with wide implications for the entire region. According to the United Nations, nearly 7 million Syrians are in need of humanitarian assistance, of whom 3 million are children. Over 4 million people have been internally displaced and a further 1.4 million people have sought refuge in neighboring countries.The number of Syrians killed in the conflict has surpassed 80'000 since the uprising started two years ago.

ENDS

en.title: Maldives repeats its calls to immediately end violence in Syria
en.description: 16 May 2013, New York; The United Nations General Assembly yesterday adopted a resolution expressing grave concerns over the continuing escalation of violence in Syria and condemning ongoing widespread and systematic gross violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms. The resolution entitled…
en.body:
16 May 2013, New York; The United Nations General Assembly yesterday adopted a resolution expressing grave concerns over the continuing escalation of violence in Syria and condemning ongoing widespread and systematic gross violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms. The resolution entitled "The situation in the Syrian Arab Republic" was adopted by a vote of 107 in favour to 12 against, with 59 abstentions. The Maldives cosponsored the resolution and voted in favour of it.

President of the General Assembly Mr. Vuk JeremiÄ‡, - along with many other speakers - highlighted that 80,000 Syrians had been killed in the violence and that 5.5 million have been displaced either internally or as refugees. In emphasizing the need for decisive action, he said that "it is high time to say enough is enough."

The resolution demandsthe immediate cessation of all violence against unarmed civilians, calls for an inclusive Syrian-led political transition to a democratic political system, supports for the work of the Joint Special Representative, calls on Syrian authorities to grant immediate, safe, full and unimpeded access to humanitarian personnel and supplies. And lastly, the resolution repeats the international community's call to all sides of the conflict to respect international human rights and international humanitarian law.

Since the beginning of the Syrianconflict, the Maldives has repeatedly and publicly condemned the grave violations by both sides and called for immediate cessation of violence. As a member of the Organisation of Islamic Countries (OIC) the Maldives joined its calls for a peaceful political solution to the crisis. Speaking at the OIC Summit in Cairo last February, His Excellency President Dr. Mohamed Waheed stated, "The government in Syria has to recognise that the civilised world will not tolerate a government killing its own people. The government in Syria has to also understand that the international community will continue to provide moral and material support for the forces of democratic change. And it has to recognise that the current wave of democratic change is unstoppable and irreversible".

By cosponsoring yesterday's resolution the Maldives has once again stood by the people of Syria and its partners within the Arab Group. The Government has also maintained a consistent policy of advocacy for the safety and rights of the Syrian people, and have made its voice heard at the General Assembly in New York, the Human Rights Council in Geneva and the OIC.

This is the fifth resolution on the situation in Syria by the General Assembly since 2011.

ENDS.

en.title: High Commissioner Naseer Presents his Letter of Credence to Indian President
en.description: 09 May 2013, Male'; New High Commissioner of Maldives to India, H. E. Mr. Mohamed Naseer presented his letter of credence to the President of India H. E. Shri. Puranab Mukherjee this morning.
en.body:
09 May 2013, Male'; New High Commissioner of Maldives to India, H. E. Mr. Mohamed Naseer presented his letter of credence to the President of India H. E. Shri. Puranab Mukherjee this morning.

President Mukherjee congratulated the new High Commissioner meeting High Commissioner Naseer at the ceremony held at the Presidential Palace to present the credentials, after which the Indian President and the High Commissioner discussed bilateral relations that exist between the two countries and ways to further strengthen these ties. President Mukherjee assured that India will continue to assist and corporate with the Maldives in all areas it needs.

High Commissioner Naseer thanked the President for all the assistance that India had provided to the Maldives in the past and reassured President Mukherjee that relations between the Maldives and India will continue to flourish. He stressed that it was his highest priority to further strengthen relations between the two countries.

ENDS.

en.title: UN's Special Representative for Violence against Children ends visit to the Maldives
en.description: 8 May 2013, Male'; The UN Secretary General's Special Representative for Violence against Children Ms. Marta Santos-Pais has ended her 5-day official trip to the Maldives.
en.body:
8 May 2013, Male'; The UN Secretary General's Special Representative for Violence against Children Ms. Marta Santos-Pais has ended her 5-day official trip to the Maldives.

Ms. Santos-Pais arrived in the Maldives on the 3rd of this month and during her stay she had conducted extensive consultations with local stakeholders including Government Ministries, the judiciary, political parties and visited the Child Care Facility on the island of Villingili. As per her mandate, Ms. Santos-Pais had focused her visit on understanding the national child protection mechanism and identifying the gaps within.

Before concluding her visit, the Special Representative held a de-briefing to the Government which was attended by the Minister of Gender, Family and Human Rights Ms. Azima Shakoor, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Ms. Dunya Maumoon and senior officials of the Gender Ministry and Foreign Ministry. Ms. Santos-Pais also held a joint briefing, together with Minister Azima, for members of the press later in the afternoon in which she shared her findings with the media. In her remarks, Ms. Santos Pais noted the need to build capacity of professionals serving in the protection system and emphasized the need to pass some of the key bills in Parliament that would strengthen the legal framework surrounding children's rights. She also identified the need to sensitize the public on child abuse issues and suggested the designing of an information dissemination strategy that would raise societal awareness. The Special Representative further laid emphasis on the need for all political leaders and parties to put children's issues first and highlighted that partisan politics should not adversely affect the reforms urgently required to the national child protection system of the country.

In her remarks at the press briefing Minister Azima thanked the Special Representative for her constructive visit and the engagement she had maintained with all local stakeholders. Commenting on the findings of Ms. Santos-Pais, the Minister concurred on the urgent need to fill the existing gaps in the child protection system including the enactment of important bills that would enhance the protection of children's rights in the Maldives. Minister Azima expressed Government's commitment to eliminate violence against children and to consolidate the protection system.

Ms. Marta Santos-Pais was seen off at the airport by the Permanent Secretary of the Foreign Ministry Mr. Hassan Shifau and members of the UN Country Team in the Maldives.

ENDS.

en.title: UN Assistant Secretary General visits Maldives
en.description: 06th May 2013, Male'; The Assistant Secretary General (ASG) for Political Affairs of the United Nations Mr. Oscar Fernandez-Taranco arrived in the Maldives this afternoon, on a three-day official visit.
en.body:
06th May 2013, Male'; The Assistant Secretary General (ASG) for Political Affairs of the United Nations Mr. Oscar Fernandez-Taranco arrived in the Maldives this afternoon, on a three-day official visit.

The ASG was welcomed at the airport by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ms. Dunya Maumoon and the UN Resident Coordinator in the Maldives Mr. Tony Lisle.

During his stay in the Maldives the Assistant Secretary General is scheduled to interact with local political stakeholders. To this effect he is scheduled to meet with His Excellency President Dr. Mohamed Waheed, key Ministers, Speaker of the Majlis, Elections Commission and political parties.In his meetings Mr. Taranco is expected to share information and exchange ideas on how best the United Nations could provide assistance to the upcoming Presidential elections.He will begin his meetings with a call on the Minister of Foreign Affairs tomorrow morning.

Mr. Taranco's visit forms part of the ongoing engagement between the Government and the United Nations. Under this engagement the ASG has visited the Maldives twice previously.ial change, and to achieve effective progress".

ENDS

en.title: Assistant Secretary General of the United Nations Calls on Foreign Minister
en.description: 6 May 2013, Male'; The Assistant Secretary General of the United Nations Mr. Oscar Fernandez-Taranco called on the Minister of Foreign Affairs H E Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah today.
en.body:
6 May 2013, Male'; The Assistant Secretary General of the United Nations Mr. Oscar Fernandez-Taranco called on the Minister of Foreign Affairs H E Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah today.

Discussions at the meeting focused on the current political developments in the country and the ongoing Maldives-UN partnership in the developmental process. Speaking during the meeting the Assistant Secretary General expressed the support of the United Nations to all efforts towards the Presidential Elections and emphasized the importance of national dialogue amongst all political parties. In response Minister Samad thanked the ASG for his constructive engagement in the Maldives and expressed appreciation to the UN's continued cooperation with the Government. The two officials also exchanged views on the structural challenges that exist in the local political landscape and discussed the reform measures needed in this regard.

The meeting which was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs was attended by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ms Dunya Maumoon and Additional Secretary Mr. Ali Naseer Mohamed. Mr. Fernandez-Taranco was accompanied by UN Resident Coordinator and other officials from the UN Country Team.

ENDS

en.title: UN's Chief Child Rights Official visits Maldives
en.description: 05 May 2013, Male'; The United Nations Secretary General's Special Representative Ms. Martha Santos Pais paid a courtesy call on Minister of Foreign Affairs H E Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah this morning.
en.body:
05 May 2013, Male'; The United Nations Secretary General's Special Representative Ms. Martha Santos Pais paid a courtesy call on Minister of Foreign Affairs H E Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah this morning.

The Minister welcomed Ms. Pais to the Maldives and expressed his confidence that her timely visit would be of immense benefit to the Government. The Minister also briefed the Special Representative on the progress achieved by the country in promoting children's rights and conveyed the Government's commitment to international human rights standards and explained the work being done to align domestic laws and efforts to the Maldives' international treaty obligations. During the discussion Ms. Pais praised the Maldives' international role in promoting human rights and commended the Government's work as the Vice Chair of the Human Rights Council in Geneva.Ms. Pais also highlighted the effectiveness of SAIVAC as an apex body of SAARC. Discussions at the meeting also focused on the extensive reform required of the existing child protection system and how her mandate could assist the Government in this regard.

The meeting was attended by senior officials of the Ministry.

During her visit Ms. Pais is scheduled to hold discussions with key domestic stakeholders including Ministers and parliamentarians. She will also call on the President and is scheduled to visit the Kudakudhinge Hiyaa in Vilingili.

The mandate of the SRSG was established in 2008 and she is a global independent advocate for the prevention and elimination of all forms of violence against children. The mandate of the SRSG is premised on human rights standards and effective implementation of core international conventions. Her mandate involves "mobilizing action and political support to maintain momentum around this agenda and generates renewed concern at the harmful effects of violence on children; to promote social change, and to achieve effective progress".

ENDS

en.title: Minister launches an awareness song on "Human Trafficking"
en.description: 01 May 2013, Male'; The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah, today launched an awareness song on "Human Trafficking" in conjunction with the International Labour Day. This is part of the "Blue Ribbon Campaign: Stand Against Human Trafficking" which was launched by the Ministry on…
en.body:
01 May 2013, Male'; The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah, today launched an awareness song on "Human Trafficking" in conjunction with the International Labour Day. This is part of the "Blue Ribbon Campaign: Stand Against Human Trafficking" which was launched by the Ministry on 9January 2013, to raise awareness among the public on the issue of human trafficking in the Maldives. The campaign is designed to reach out to the general public on the causes and consequences of the crime of trafficking.

Speaking at the launching ceremony, Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah stressed on the importance of setting up mechanisms to combat human trafficking, and raising public awareness on the issue. The Minister also thanked the "Bridesmen" for compiling the music, Mr. Hassan Hilmy for the lyrics and Mr. Ibrahim Ali (Kuda Ibbe) for assisting with the sound recording.

ENDS.

en.title: New UN Chief calls on the Foreign Minister
en.description: 30 April 2013, Male'; The New Resident Coordinator of the United Nations to the Maldives Mr. Anthony (Tony) Lisle called on His Excellency Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah yesterday.
en.body:
30 April 2013, Male'; The New Resident Coordinator of the United Nations to the Maldives Mr. Anthony (Tony) Lisle called on His Excellency Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah yesterday.

In the meeting that took place at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Samad welcomed Mr. Lisle to the Maldives and expressed confidence in his leadership to achieve a more successful Maldives-UN partnership. Minister Samad also briefed Mr. Lisle on the political developments and the upcoming Presidential elections.

In his remarks Mr. Lisle congratulated the Maldives for its leadership in the United Nations and especially at the Human Rights Council. He also praised the Maldives "outstanding contributions" to the international human rights mechanisms.

The new Resident Coordinator briefed on UN assistance programme and UN engagement with the Government and focused on the progress by the Maldives in achieving the MDG's. Discussions also focused on the UN's ongoing engagement with the Government in relation to political and technical issues and other key areas of cooperation.

Mr. Tony Lisle is Australian by nationality and was based in Viet Nam as UNAIDS Country Director prior to his appointment in the Maldives.He was responsible for leading, coordinating and facilitating an expanded Joint UN system response to HIV in Viet Nam. He also served as UNAIDS Country Coordinator in Cambodia and as Regional Advisor on HIV/AIDS for UNICEF based in Geneva. Mr. Lisle's also served in Thailand and Laos.

ENDS

en.title: New Afghan Ambassador Presents Credentials to the President
en.description: 29 April 2013, Male'; New Ambassador of Afghanistan accredited to the Maldives, Shaida Mohammaad Abdali presented his letter of credence to President Dr Mohamed Waheed this morning.
en.body:
29 April 2013, Male'; New Ambassador of Afghanistan accredited to the Maldives, Shaida Mohammaad Abdali presented his letter of credence to President Dr Mohamed Waheed this morning.

At the ceremony held at the President's Office to present the credentials, President Waheed congratulated Ambassador Abdali. en.title: Minister Samad meets with Parliamentary Under Secretary of State for Foreign and Commonwealth Affairs
en.description: 26 April 2013, London, UK; TheMinister of Foreign Affairs Dr Abdul Samad Abdulla yesterday met with Mr Alistair Burt MP, Parliamentary Secretary of State for Foreign and Commonwealth Affairs.
en.body:
26 April 2013, London, UK; TheMinister of Foreign Affairs Dr Abdul Samad Abdulla yesterday met with Mr Alistair Burt MP, Parliamentary Secretary of State for Foreign and Commonwealth Affairs.

At the meeting Minister Samad briefed Minister Burt on the progress the Government of Maldives had made in strengthening democratic institutions in the country. Dr Samad expressed his sincere gratitude to Minister Burt and the UK Government for their continued engagement and assistance with Institution building in the Maldives.

Minister Samad also spoke of the problems Maldivian students accepted to study in the UK face in obtaining visas, especially the issue of travelling to Colombo to obtain UK student visa.

"The Government hopes a permanent solution to this problem can be sought as it is hindering the nation's youth from obtaining the exceptional quality of higher education offered by UK universities. Without a permanent solution, Maldivian students will increasingly be forced to seek alternative sources of higher education. This regrettable outcome is in neither of our countries' interests"

Minister Burt expressed his hope that the UK Government would find a solution to this problem and reaffirmed the British Governments commitment to the Maldivian people. Mr Burt stated that the UK had always and will continue to be a close development partner of the Maldives both bilaterally and through the Commonwealth.

During the meeting Dr Samad also briefed Minister Burt on the ongoing preparations for the upcoming Presidential elections. Minister Samad concluded the meeting by expressing the Maldivian Governments commitment to strengthening democracy in the country noting that this could only be done with the continued constructive engagement and support of the international community.

ENDS

en.title: Minister meets with the Chair of the All-Party British-Maldives Parliamentary Group

26 April 2013, Male'; The Minister of Foreign Affairs Dr. Abdul Samad Abdulla yesterday met with Mr. David Amess MP, Chair of the All-Party British-Maldives Parliamentary Group as part of his official visit to the United Kingdom.

Dr. Samad thanked Mr. Amess for the continued support the APPG had shown the Government anddiscussed ways in which the relationship between Maldivian Parliamentarians and Members of Parliament in the UK could be further strengthened.

Mr. Amess stated that the All Party Group had always taken a keen interest in issues pertinent to the Maldives and was hopeful that it would continue to provide assistance to the Government in this regard. Mr. Amess also expressed his beliefthat an exchange of dialogue between British and Maldivian Parliamentarians would be an effective way of strengthening Parliamentary institutions in the Maldives.

en.title: CMAG Foreign Ministers welcome Maldives' return to CMAG
en.description: 26 April 2013, London;The Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group (CMAG) today welcomed the return of Maldives as a fully participating member of the Group. Today's meeting, held at the Commonwealth Secretariat in London, was the first scheduled meeting to take place since CMAG decided to permit…
en.body:
26 April 2013, London;The Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group (CMAG) today welcomed the return of Maldives as a fully participating member of the Group. Today's meeting, held at the Commonwealth Secretariat in London, was the first scheduled meeting to take place since CMAG decided to permit Maldives' return to the Group at its meeting in September 2012.

Resuming Maldives' place on CMAG, Minister of Foreign Affairs Dr Abdul Samad joined Commonwealth Secretary-General Mr Kamalesh Sharma, and the Foreign Ministers of Australia, Bangladesh, Canada, Jamaica, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, Trinidad and Tobago and Vanuatu to discuss the pressing issues on the CMAG agenda.

Foreign Minister Samad actively contributed to CMAG discussions and thanked the Commonwealth Secretary General and CMAG Foreign Ministers for their constructive engagement with Maldives last year.

Speaking earlier this week, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Dunya Maumoon said that Maldives' invitation to return to CMAG reflected the Commonwealth's recognition of the cooperation of President Dr Mohamed Waheed's government in strengthening democracy in the Maldives.

CMAG is comprised of the foreign ministers of eight Commonwealth countries and deals with serious and persistent violations of the Commonwealth's fundamental political values. CMAG's main task is to assess infringements and recommend measures to restore democracy and constitutional rule.

External Link:

Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group Concluding Statement, London, 26 April 2013

ENDS

en.title: First Non- Resident Ambassador to the Republic of Korea presents Credentials
en.description: 22 April 2013, Male';The first Non- Resident Ambassador of the Republic of Maldives accredited to the Republic of Korea His Excellency Mr. Ahmed Khaleel, has presented his Letter of Credence to the President of the Republic of Korea, Her Excellency Ms. Park Geun-hye in a ceremony held at the Cheong…
en.body:
22 April 2013, Male';The first Non- Resident Ambassador of the Republic of Maldives accredited to the Republic of Korea His Excellency Mr. Ahmed Khaleel, has presented his Letter of Credence to the President of the Republic of Korea, Her Excellency Ms. Park Geun-hye in a ceremony held at the Cheong Wa Dae (Blue House) in Seoul on 18 April 2013.

During the meeting which followed the Ceremony, President Park congratulated Ambassador Khaleel on his accreditation as the first Maldivian Ambassador to Korea and expressed confidence that this will lead to further strengthening of the friendly relations between the Maldives and the Republic of Korea. Ambassador Khaleel thanked the President for the warm welcome and conveyed greetings from H.E. President Dr. Mohamed Waheed and the people of the Maldives.

Ambassador Khaleel also conveyed the sincere appreciation of the Government and the people of the Maldives for the continued assistance and cooperation from the Republic of Korea to the Maldives. Continuing, the Ambassador highlighted the threats faced by the Maldives due to global warming and environmental degradation and expressed the wish of the Maldives to continue to work with the Republic of Korea to find a comprehensive and binding agreement to curb climate change.

Speaking on the current issue in the Korean Peninsula, Ambassador Khaleel assured President Park of the support of the Government of the Maldives to the Republic of Korea as it strives to find a peaceful resolution to the ongoing tensions in the Peninsula.

Ambassador Khaleel also highlighted that Maldives places importance on the promotion of investments and economic cooperation between the two countries. President Park assured the Ambassador of the readiness of Korea to work with the Maldives to further enhance relations between the two countries in this regard. The President also noted that the Maldives is one of the most popular tourist destinations for young Koreans and expressed her hope that the recently inaugurated scheduled air services between the two countries will help more Koreans to travel to the Maldives on their honeymoon.

During the visit to Seoul, Ambassador Khaleel also called on the senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea and held meetings with some potential Korean investors.

H.E. Mr. Ahmed Khaleel is concurrently accredited to Japan and is based in Tokyo. The Embassy of the Maldives in Tokyo will be responsible for relations with the Republic of Korea as well.

en.title: President Sends a Message of Sympathy to the US President
en.description: 16 April 2013, Male'; President Dr Mohamed Waheed has sent a message of sympathy to President of the United State of America Barack Obama, following the deadly explosions at the Boston Marathon.
en.body:
16 April 2013, Male'; President Dr Mohamed Waheed has sent a message of sympathy to President of the United State of America Barack Obama, following the deadly explosions at the Boston Marathon.

The President's message to the US President reads as follows:

"The Government and the people of the Maldives and I are deeply shocked and horrified to learn about the deadly twin explosions at the Boston marathon, causing tragic loss of lives and grievous injury to many. The Government and people of the Maldives strongly condemn this cowardly act of terror in the strongest terms, and we express our firm solidarity with the United States of America in all its efforts in maintaining peace and harmony."

"The Maldives stands firm in its commitment to the fight against the global menace of terrorism. The world has stood witness to the suffering and pain caused by terrorism, undermining the achievements of our present day as we strive towards a better global order. It is thus, imperative that the international community as a whole work towards eliminating the scourge of terrorism"

"Today's attacks only serve to remind us that the world can no longer linger blindly to the tragedies engulfing our innocent people. Ours is a time for committed and positive action, and at this time of national tragedy, we pledge our full support and extend our deep sympathy to you, to the people and Government of United States of America. Please also convey our sincere condolences to the members of the bereaved families"

ENDS.

en.description: 09 April 2013, Male'; We would like to thank the international community for their concern in the case of the 15 year old girl who recently received a flogging sentence here in the Maldives. en.body:
09 April 2013, Male'; We would like to thank the international community for their concern in the case of the 15 year old girl who recently received a flogging sentence here in the Maldives. Currently the case is being appealed and I have urged the judiciary to resolve this matter as quickly as possible. This case should never have been presented in the courts and we are working to ensure that cases like this are never brought to the courts again.

The young woman remains under the care of the Ministry of Gender, Family and Human Rights, my Attorney General has met with her and she is receiving the appropriate physical and psychological counseling at this time. We appreciate the international compassion for this young woman and ask for your patience as this case moves through the judicial system. As both the President and as a father, I am fully committed to protecting and advancing the rights of women and girls in the Maldives and throughout the world and share your deep concern about this young victim.

The Maldives is a young democracy working to balance our religious faith with our new democratic values. I ask that you support us and join us as partners as we work through this challenge. A boycott on tourism will only serve as a setback to the economic opportunities and rights we are all striving to uphold for women, girls and the hardworking Maldivian people in general.

ENDS.

en.title: 22nd Session of the Human Rights Council Concludes with the Adoption of a Number of Important Resolutions
en.description: 25March 2013, Geneva; The UN Human Rights Council has concluded its 22nd session in Geneva, with the adoption of a number of resolutions on the rights of the child, prevention of torture,protecting human rights defenders,the role of parliamentarians in the work of the Council and country specific…
en.body:
25March 2013, Geneva; The UN Human Rights Council has concluded its 22nd session in Geneva, with the adoption of a number of resolutions on the rights of the child, prevention of torture,protecting human rights defenders,the role of parliamentarians in the work of the Council and country specific human rights situations in Syria and also in Sri Lanka.

The session began on 25th February with the Opening Statement by the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights H.E. Navanethem Pillay, taking stock of the situation of human rights around the world and elaborated on a number of important thematic areas of concern which the Council should consider in its deliberations. The Maldives delegation to the 22nd Session was led by H.E. Dr Mariyam Shakeela, Minister for Environment and Energy. She was accompanied to the Human Rights Council by H.E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs. In her opening address to the Council, Minister Shakeela, identified fundamental elements in the work of the Council for the Maldives to take note of, and reiterated the Government's commitment to promote and protect human rights in the country. The delegation also launched the re-election campaign of the Maldives to the Human Rights Council for the term 2014-2016.

The Maldives followed closely a number of key resolutions in the Council and actively took part in negotiations on Syria, the role of parliamentarians and also on the resolution on combating intolerance. The Maldives supported Sri Lanka, on the resolution which was tabled in the Council by the United States focusing on the situation of human rights in that country. The Maldives also supported all Palestinian resolutions in the Council, and spoke in favour of the plight of the Palestinian people in the Occupied Territories.

en.description: 24 March 2013, Male';Canadian Special Envoy to the Commonwealth, Senator Hugh Segal has met the His Excellency Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah, Minister of Foreign Affairs today. The call was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
en.body:
24 March 2013, Male';Canadian Special Envoy to the Commonwealth, Senator Hugh Segal has met the His Excellency Dr. Abdul Samad Abdullah, Minister of Foreign Affairs today. The call was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Foreign Minister Samad welcomed the Senator and highlighted the close relations between the two countries and expressed appreciation for the assistance received from Canada especially in the area of human resource development. Minister Samad briefed the Senator on the current political situation and affirmed the Government's commitment to work with international partners in strengthening the democratic process.

Senator Segal thanked the Minister and expressed confidence that the relations between the two countries will continue to strengthen. He stated that Canada fully accepts all CoNI findings and wishes to have constructive engagement with the Maldives.

The meeting was also attended by Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Mr. Abdul Azeez Yoosuf, Ambassador and senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

ENDS.

en.title: Statement by the Government of Maldives
en.description: 16 March 2013, Male' The Government of the Maldives considers the ‘Declaration' issued on the Maldives by the European Union's High Representative, Catherine Ashton, on 14 March 2013, as unfortunate and unacceptable. The Government is committed to ensuring that the Presidential elections will be…
en.body:
16 March 2013, Male'

The Government of the Maldives considers the ‘Declaration' issued on the Maldives by the European Union's High Representative, Catherine Ashton, on 14 March 2013, as unfortunate and unacceptable. The Government is committed to ensuring that the Presidential elections will be fair and inclusive of all qualified parties and individuals wishing to participate.

It must be noted that the criminal charges filed against former President Mr. Mohamed Nasheed by the independent Prosecutor General concerns the arrest and detention of a sitting judge of a superior court in the Maldives in January 2012. President Nasheed disregarded over a dozen court orders from the Civil Court, Criminal Court, High Court and the Supreme Court to produce the Judge before the court. President Nasheed also dismissed calls by the Human Rights Commission of the Maldives, Prosecutor General, and several international organisations, including the EU, to release the judge.

Moreover, under the 2008 Constitution, the Executive branch of the Government cannot intervene in a case filed by the Prosecutor General (PG). The PG in fact ordered the investigation of the case, in January 2012, while President Nasheed was still the President.

The Court's decision earlier this month to postpone Mr. Nasheed's trial clearly shows that the courts in the Maldives are in fact able to make credible decisions in a politically divisive environment and that they are neither unfairly biased against Mr. Nasheed nor conspiring against him. The decision also goes on to highlight that the case against the former President is not politically motivated and that in effect, Mr. Nasheed does accept that there is a genuine case against him. The Government has always maintained that it should be given the necessary space to manage and develop an authentic democratic culture in the Maldives without external interference.

It is therefore regrettable that a responsible international organisation, such as the EU, chose to state in public that the forthcoming presidential elections would not be credible unless a particular person is allowed to contest in the elections. It is important to note that elections in the Maldives are held in accordance with the Constitution and the relevant laws of the Maldives. The Government in the Maldives is elected by the people and for the people of the Maldives.

ENDS.

en.title: Maldives at the Human Rights Council
en.description: 11 March 2013, Male';At the 22nd Session of the Human Rights Council, currently ongoing in Geneva, the Maldives delegation has been actively participating in the debate and negotiations of the Council. The Maldives Delegation in Geneva is led by Ambassador Iruthisham Adam.
en.body:
11 March 2013, Male';At the 22nd Session of the Human Rights Council, currently ongoing in Geneva, the Maldives delegation has been actively participating in the debate and negotiations of the Council. The Maldives Delegation in Geneva is led by Ambassador Iruthisham Adam.

The Maldives as a Vice Chair of the Council has the opportunity to contribute to the discussions of the Bureau of the Council. To this effect, the Maldives Ambassador exchanged views with the UN Secretary General Mr. Ban Ki-Moo, during the Secretary General's first historic meeting with the President and Bureau of the Council. During the discussion, Ambassador Adam emphasized the need to strengthen technical support to Small Island Developing Countries & LDCs and the need for a more balanced geographical representation of staff at the OHCHR and noted that the Asian region is largely underrepresented in the Office.

The Maldives represents the Asian Group in the Bureau of the Council.

Continuing to play a strong role during the third year of the membership, the Maldives Delegation participated in discussions on thematic areas of human rights and environment, the rights of children and the rights of disabled persons. In addition the Maldives responded to the Annual report of the High Commissioner for Human Rights and took part in the high level debate on Mainstreaming of Human Rights. The Maldives used the opportunity to update the Council on the current political developments in the country and the efforts underway to consolidate the national human rights framework. The Maldives requested the expert opinion of the Panelists on how democracies in transition could effectively strengthen their domestic human rights framework.

Similarly the Maldives participated in the Annual Thematic Discussion on Disability wherein the Maldives delegation called for states to adopt measures geared towards increasing economic opportunities for persons with disability. Noting that a disabled person has a 50% chance of being unemployed, while others with the same merit and qualification has 80% chance of getting an employment the Maldives highlighted that the main challenge for the country at present was combating the stigma attached and stereotyping of disabled persons that leads to them being labeled as unworthy of any economic opportunity within society. The Maldives also explored how the introduction of quotas for the disabled and concessions for employers who employ disabled persons and easy access into micro-credit schemes for the disabled would help overcome the current situation in the country.

During the interactive dialogue with thematic mandate holders the Maldives extended an invitation to the Human Rights Council's Independent Expert on Human Rights and Environment, Professor John Knox to visit the Maldives. Professor Knox is the Human Rights Council's first-ever mandate-holder on the wider question of human rights and environment, the mandate of which was spearheaded by the Maldives Delegation in 2011 which culminated in the establishment of the mandate by consensus in March 2012. During the Interactive Dialogue with the Independent Expert the Maldives welcomed Professor Knox's first report wherein he conceptualised the issue of human rights and the right to a healthy environment. In its statement the Maldives requested that the linkages between the right to a healthy environment and its impact on vulnerable groups such as women and children be explored by the Expert in his future reports. The Delegation also posed the issue of climate change being inherently linked to the mandate's theme and requested that it be further looked at in the next report of the Expert.

The Maldives also participated in the negotiations of draft resolutions presented to the current Session, particularly those relating to the Maldives' priority areas in Geneva. In this regard, the Maldives co-sponsored the Joint Statements on various topics including the Financing of the OHCHR, Mainstreaming of Human Rights, Situation in Syria, Truth and Reconciliation and Marking of International Women's Day. Lastly the Delegation attended several informal consultations on a variety of human rights related issues such as defamation of Islam, promotion of peaceful protests, prevention of torture and the protection of human rights defenders.

ENDS.

en.title: President Appoints High Commissioner to India
en.description: 10 March 2013, Male'; President Dr. Mohamed Waheed has appointed Mr. Mohamed Naseer as the High Commissioner of Maldives to India.
en.body:
10 March 2013, Male'; President Dr. Mohamed Waheed has appointed Mr. Mohamed Naseer as the High Commissioner of Maldives to India.

The presentation of letter of appointment to Mr. Naseer was held this afternoon at the President's Office.

Speaking at the function, President Waheed congratulated the new High Commissioner. The President also expressed confidence that High Commissioner Naseer would protect and promote the interest of the people of Maldives, and work to enhance cooperation between the Maldives and India.

ENDS.

en.title: Commonwealth Day Message by Minister
en.description: The Commonwealth Day is an opportunity to celebrate the Commonwealth principles and values. The modern Commonwealth, which came into being following the London Declaration of 1949, represents one-quarter of the world's countries brought together by a commitment to shared values of equality,…
en.body:
The Commonwealth Day is an opportunity to celebrate the Commonwealth principles and values. The modern Commonwealth, which came into being following the London Declaration of 1949, represents one-quarter of the world's countries brought together by a commitment to shared values of equality, democracy, good governance, the rule of law, and the protection of human rights. These values and principles, most clearly articulated in the 2009 Affirmation, would continue to guide the member-States of the Commonwealth in their strive to improve the lives of their peoples. The values also help the Commonwealth and its member-States in building national resilience, a theme of the 2011 Commonwealth Summit in Perth, Australia.

This year's Commonwealth Day theme, Opportunity through Enterprise,highlights the critical importance of protecting and promoting the core values of the Commonwealth. Human innovation, particularly entrepreneurial innovation, could thrive only in an environment where human rights are fully protected, where individual freedom is guaranteed, and where the rule of law is upheld. It is precisely the type of environment that the Maldives is striving to create in the country with a democratic reform programme that began a few years back. While the democratisation programme brings with it challenges, it also creates enormous opportunities for empowering youth, women, and men so that they become more enterprising individuals. The Commonwealth is ideally placed to become a partner with emerging democracies like the Maldives in designing and implementing programmes that create opportunities through enterprise. For, it is such continued and close partnership, as opposed to public statements that criticise the democratic institutions of a country that can help to cultivate and nurture the values of democracy in a society.

We celebrate the Commonwealth Day, because we cherish the Commonwealth's core values and principles, which, we believe, are worth promoting at national and global levels. We value our membership in the organisation because the Commonwealth has a large number of small states, and the organisation plays an important and visible role in highlighting the vulnerabilities of small states in global politics.

As such the Commonwealth should not be allowed to be used as an arena by some to target small states such as the Maldives; especially at a time when the country is at its most vulnerable stage in democratic transition. It is important that the Commonwealth uphold its principles of democracy and equality within the organisation to ensure that it is used as a forum that positively benefits all member states. The Commonwealth, therefore, is in need of urgent reform to make it a more relevant association for all its members, irrespective of size. The Maldives would continue to work with other member States in its efforts to bring the necessary reforms to the Commonwealth and its working methods to ensure that the organisation is not used by anyone as an instrument to promote their own political interests.

The Maldives calls upon the Commonwealth to give true meaning to the principles enshrined in the new Commonwealth Charter; principles of democracy, human rights, rule of law, separation of powers and good governance.

ENDS.

en.title: Former President Nasheed under Police custody:- Updated Information
en.description: 06 March 2013, Male'; Former President Mohamed Nasheed was brought under Police custody yesterday afternoon, following a court order issued by the Hulhumale Magistrate Court, that instructed the Maldives Police Service to produce the former President to court today at 1600 hours. Updated…
en.body:
06 March 2013, Male'; Former President Mohamed Nasheed was brought under Police custody yesterday afternoon, following a court order issued by the Hulhumale Magistrate Court, that instructed the Maldives Police Service to produce the former President to court today at 1600 hours. Updated information from the MPS confirms that Mr. Nasheed was brought under custody while on Rahdhebai Magu, near the Centre for Higher Secondary Education (CHSE). The Court order was read to him while taking him into custody.

Mr. Nasheed continued to walk under Police escort and boarded a police speed boat, near the Police Headquarters. He was taken to Dhoonidhoo island, where he is at present.

Access to Mr. Nasheed's lawyers were granted to him later in the afternoon.

In a press briefing held last evening around 1900 hours, the Police showed a video of Mr. Nasheed being brought under Police custody. It also showed the Police reading the court order to him.

ENDS.

en.title: Former President Nasheed's Trial Postponed: Updated Information
en.description: 6 March 2013, Male'; The Hulhumale Magistrate Court has decided today to postpone the trial of former President Mohamed Nasheed for four weeks. The court's decision came following Mr. Nasheed's legal counsel's request in the court to postpone the case either for four weeks or until the Presidential…
en.body:
6 March 2013, Male'; The Hulhumale Magistrate Court has decided today to postpone the trial of former President Mohamed Nasheed for four weeks. The court's decision came following Mr. Nasheed's legal counsel's request in the court to postpone the case either for four weeks or until the Presidential elections.

After deliberations by the bench, the court decided to postpone the case for four weeks, on the request by the former President, as the Elections Commission had not yet formally declared the candidates of the election. The court, however, did mention that once the candidacy was announced formally, they would consider the matter again.

Presidential elections are slated for September this year.

ENDS

en.title: Former President Nasheed Brought Under Police Custody
en.description: 05 March 2013, Male'; The Hulhumale Magistrate Court today issued an order to the Maldives Police Service to produce former President Mohamed Nasheed to the court at 1600 hours, on Wednesday, 6 March 2013. According to the Police Service, the Police went to Mr. Nasheed's residence G. Kenereege…
en.body:
05 March 2013, Male'; The Hulhumale Magistrate Court today issued an order to the Maldives Police Service to produce former President Mohamed Nasheed to the court at 1600 hours, on Wednesday, 6 March 2013. According to the Police Service, the Police went to Mr. Nasheed's residence G. Kenereege around 1330 hours this afternoon and showed him the court order. Nevertheless, Mr. Nasheed refused to receive the court order. Hence, the Police confirmed the existence of the court order verbally to President Nasheed. The former President then volunteered to walk to the Police Headquarters.

Mr. Nasheed is currently under police custody in the island of Dhoonidhoo near Male'.

The Maldives Police Service confirmed that Mr. Nasheed has been given access to his lawyers and the Police had informed the Police Integrity Commission and the Human Rights Commission of his custody.

ENDS.

en.title: Maldives Reaffirms Commitment to Ratify the Child Rights Protocol
en.description: 3 March 2013, New York; The Maldives participated at a panel discussion last week, which was aimed at promoting the ratification of the Third Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child on a Communications Procedures. During the one-year anniversary of the opening for Optional…
en.body:
3 March 2013, New York; The Maldives participated at a panel discussion last week, which was aimed at promoting the ratification of the Third Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child on a Communications Procedures. During the one-year anniversary of the opening for Optional Protocol for signature, the Maldives reaffirmed and reiterated its commitment to promote and protect the rights of children, especially that of the girl child.

Speaking at the event, H.E. Mr. Ahmed Sareer, Permanent Representative of the Republic of Maldives to the United Nations mentioned that the individual complaints procedure was an important tool for the Maldives and other developing countries, and expressed the Government's hope that the Protocol would enter into force at the earliest possible opportunity.

He also outlined the latest developments in the recent case involving a 15 year-old girl. He mentioned that the Government is currently looking to facilitate the appeal of the case through the defendant's legal counsel and that it believed that she is a victim of sexual abuse and should be treated as such by the State and the society, and therefore her rights should be fully protected. Mr. Sareer noted that for the Government, the Court's verdict had highlighted the critical need to review existing mechanisms on child rights, and to update and improve existing measures, especially the legal framework.

The panel discussion was organized by an international coalition of non-governmental organizations supporting the rapid ratification and early entry into force of the Optional Protocol. The Maldives was a co-sponsor of the event along with the delegations of Finland, Germany, Liechtenstein and Thailand.

The Third Optional Protocol on a communications procedure was adopted by the General Assembly in December 2011, which allows the Committee on the Rights o the Child to receive and examine individual complaints alleging violation of children's rights. The Maldives signed the Optional Protocol on 28 February 2012 in Geneva, Switzerland.

ENDS

en.title: Sentencing of Flogging a 15-year-old Sexual Abuse Victim is Deeply Concerning: Government of Maldives
en.description: 28 February 2013, Malé;The Government of Maldives is deeply concerned by the prosecution and the Juvenile Court's sentence to flog a 15 year-old girl on the charges of pre-marital sex. Though the flogging will be deferred until the girl turns 18, the Government believes she is the victim of sexual…
en.body:
28 February 2013, Malé;The Government of Maldives is deeply concerned by the prosecution and the Juvenile Court's sentence to flog a 15 year-old girl on the charges of pre-marital sex. Though the flogging will be deferred until the girl turns 18, the Government believes she is the victim of sexual abuse and should be treated as such by the State and the society and therefore, her rights should be fully protected. The Government is of the view that the case merits appeal. The girl is under State care and the Government will facilitate and supervise her appeal of the case, via the girl's lawyer, to ensure that justice is done and her rights are protected.

The rights of children are protected under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and corresponding domestic legislation in the Maldives. Protecting the rights of the child, particularly that of the girl child, has always been a top priority of the Government, not only in this Administration, but previous Administrations as well.The Juvenile Court's verdict has brought home the critical and severe need to review existing mechanisms, especially legal framework, available for protecting the rights of the children in the Maldives.

Although the Maldives heralded a modern new democratic Constitution in 2008, much of the corresponding legislation aimed at reforming the criminal justice system and the juvenile justice system remains. While the Act on Special Measures for Perpetrators of Child Sexual Abuse was enacted in 2009, a large number of Bills remain pending that are essential to reform the criminal justice sector. This includes the Criminal Procedure Code, the Amendments to the Child Rights Act as well as the revised Penal Code and the Juvenile Justice Bill. The Government therefore calls on the Parliament to pass these Bills urgently.

The Government also calls on all stakeholders to view cases of child abuse and child-sexual abuse through a human rights lens and to base each case on the best interest of the child.

In view of the urgent attention required for protecting the rights of the children, the Government has established a Committee to review the existing child protection mechanisms, particularly the legal mechanism, in view of the universally accepted norms and principles, and recommend to the State areas that require urgent changes. The Committee comprises the Ministry of Gender, Family, and Human Rights, the Attorney General's Office, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Islamic Affairs, and the Family Protection Authority of Maldives.

END

en.title: Maldives Launches its Re-election Campaign in Geneva
en.description: 27 February 2013, Geneva' The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs H E Dunya Maumoon, has kick-started the Maldives' campaign for re-election to the Human Rights Council, in Geneva.
en.body:
27 February 2013, Geneva' The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs H E Dunya Maumoon, has kick-started the Maldives' campaign for re-election to the Human Rights Council, in Geneva.

At the launching ceremony held at the Palais des Nations yesterday, the State Minister introduced the Maldives' Story in which she narrated the country's journey in the Council and the issues it had played a leading role in. She noted that the Maldives' was the smallest country ever to sit on the Council but that it had never hesitated in taking strong positions on any issues including the controversial ones and in advocating for small states-related issues.

The Maldives had prioritised its term in the Council by focusing on women and children's rights and the rights of persons with disability, had been a vocal campaigner for the prevention of torture, and brought the issue of the right of all to live in a safe and clean environment to the forefront of the Council's debate. In its two-year term, the Maldives has also championed the issue of the inherent link between human rights and climate change and run consecutive and consensus based resolutions that had received support from all regions. In Mach 2012, the Maldives established an Independent Expert on Human Rights and Environment to contribute to the Council's discourse and debates on the matter.

In her remarks yesterday, the State Minister committed the Maldives support to strengthening its infant democracy and to all nations undergoing democratic change around the world and noted the important role of the Council in this effort.

The launching event was attended by 150 delegates including visiting Ministers, Ambassadors, NGOs and UN Officials attending the Human Rights Council. The event was introduced by Ambassador of Maldives in Geneva, H E Ms Iruthisham Adam.

The election to choose new members to the Council will be held in October / November 2013, at the 68th Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. At the 2010 elections, the Maldives received widespread support with 185 votes in its favour out of 192; the largest number of votes obtained till date at the Council elections.

End.

en.title: 22nd Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council Opens Today
en.description: 25 February 2013, Geneva;22nd Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council opened today, at 0900 hrs at the United Nations Office in Geneva.
en.body:
25 February 2013, Geneva;22nd Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council opened today, at 0900 hrs at the United Nations Office in Geneva.

The Maldives delegation to this Session is led by the Acting Minister for Gender, Family and Human Rights, and Minister of Environment and Energy, H.E. Dr. Mariyam Shakeela. Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, H.E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon, also attended the session.

The Council was opened by the President of the UN General Assembly, Mr. Vuk Jeremic. United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Ms. Navi Pillay, current President of the Human Rights Council, Permanent Representative of Poland, Mr. Remigiusz Achilles Henczel, Head of the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs of Switzerland, Mr. Didier Burkhalter also addressed the Opening Session.

In the High Commissioner's statement, she highlighted on the Vienna Declaration and Programme of Action, which is marking it Twentieth Anniversary this year. A High Level Panel will be held at the Human Rights Council, on this Occasion today.

As the Head of Delegation, Dr. Shakeela will be making a statement at the High Level Segment on 26 February 2013, at 1530 hrs. The delegation is scheduled to meet with High Commissioner Pillay, and other bilateral partners to discuss issues of mutual interest during the segment. State Minister Dunya Maumoon will also launch Maldives' campaign for Re-election at the United Nations Human Rights Council, for the 2014-2016, the elections of which are scheduled to be held in New York, at the 68th United Nations General Assembly, in October/November 2013.

Maldives is the smallest country ever to serve in the Council membership, and also currently holds the Vice-Presidency of the Bureau of the Human Rights Council. The Maldives seat at the Council is represented by the Permanent Mission of Maldives to the United Nations Office in Geneva, led by H.E. Ms. Iruthisham Adam, Permanent Representative / Ambassador of Maldives to the United Nations Office in Geneva.

ENDS.
